transcript:
Header: 2027-06-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Laura (Redwood SE), Maya (Astra Head of AI), Ethan (Platform), Priya (Security), Oliver (PM)

Summary: Quick discovery focusing on integration surface: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy config, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Astra is leaning toward Dedicated for predictable latency but exploring Hosted for faster MVP. Security team flagged KMS and audit log requirements. Agreed next steps include sharing integration samples and scheduling POC scoping.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intros, i'm Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. with me is laura our solutions engineer. how about you folks?
[00:22] Maya: hi all, maya here, head of ai at astra commerce. we run recommendations and search, looking at LLMs for merchant support and code gen for internal ops.
[00:34] Oliver: oliver, product, i'll own success criteria and use cases.
[00:40] Ethan: ethan, platform engineer—i'm the one who will integrate the SDK and the gateway.
[00:45] Priya: priya from security, i'll be looking at compliance and kms.
[00:50] Laura: great, thanks. objective for today is to understand your integration constraints and success metrics—sdk/llm framework support, proxy/gateway patterns, traffic profile, and observability needs.

[01:15] Maya: high level—two tracks. 1) quick hosted MVP to get merchant-facing chat and triage live within 6-8 weeks. 2) longer-term dedicated or private for production due to latency and data residency concerns.
[01:35] Samir: that's common. we usually recommend hosted to iterate quickly and then Dedicated when you need predictable throughput and isolation. laura, maybe you can give a quick overview of SDKs and builtin connectors?
[01:50] Laura: sure — Redwood has REST plus official SDKs for node/python; we also maintain connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. the langchain connector maps to Redwood chat/generate APIs and supports streaming. there are examples for retriever-based RAG with LlamaIndex, and a small repo showing prefetching K/V cache usage.
[02:15] Ethan: question — our infra uses an internal gateway (kong) and we have service mesh. what's the recommended pattern? direct SDK calls from backend, or route through our gateway?
[02:34] Laura: either works. for hosted, we see two common patterns: 1) server-side calls from your backend (recommended), where you call Redwood with your API key from a trusted env behind the gateway. 2) for client-side quick experiments, you can use short-lived tokens via a proxy. with dedicated, we typically deploy a customer-side proxy into your VPC to handle egress and mTLS.
[03:05] Maya: sounds good. what's the latency overhead if we put an internal proxy in front? our 95th p95 target for chat is ~250ms per token for merchant support flows.
[03:22] Laura: the proxy adds minimal overhead — usually single-digit ms if it's within the same region. the bigger impact is model choice and KV cache hit rate. for Redwood Dedicated we can guarantee latencies to a SLA band based on instance sizing; we'll include our performance profiles in the doc.
[03:50] Oliver: about rate limits and quotas—we have spikes during flash sales. can you do burst credit or autoscaling?
[04:02] Samir: Dedicated supports burst capacity and configurable autoscaling policies. hosted has per-account quotas; we can increase limits for known spikes and we also have rate-limit headers in responses so you can alert. laura, do we expose per-route quota config?
[04:18] Laura: yes, per-route and per-API-key quotas. we also instrument traffic per model and per-route for billing/observability. you can set hard limits or soft-throttles with fallback policies — e.g., fall back to a smaller model or cached response.
[04:42] Ethan: for our integration we'd prefer a gateway that sets a monotonic retry/backoff. how do you recommend handling 429s?
[04:52] Laura: 429s come with Retry-After headers. we recommend client-side exponential backoff and on the server side a circuit breaker that falls back to cached answers or a local cheap model. Redwood's SDKs include a retry helper that respects the headers.
[05:10] Priya: security: we need SOC2 plus audit logs for all queries and responses. can you redact PII in logs or avoid storing responses?
[05:22] Samir: hosted stores logs for a default retention; we have options to disable storing user data, and Dedicated/Private gives you control over retention and where logs live. we support KMS for envelope encryption, and we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM in Private deployments. laura, we have the security pack docs link right?
[05:38] Laura: yes — i'll share the SOC2, encryption in transit/at rest, KMS integration doc. for redaction, we provide pre- and post-processing hooks and you can configure scrubbers before logs persist.
[05:52] Maya: can you walk through observability hooks — we currently use Datadog and Sentry. we want per-prompt latency, token counts, and model-level metrics per route.
[06:06] Laura: Redwood emits structured traces and metrics. you can send traces to their APM or export via OTLP to Datadog/Jaeger. metrics include per-request token usage, latency breakdown (network, runtime, kernel), and cache hit ratio. we also include token-level cost estimates in the response metadata.
[06:28] Oliver: is there a webhook for async events like model rollouts or fallback triggers?
[06:34] Laura: yes, there are observability webhooks for route alerts, automatic fallback events, and rollout status. these can be posted to your incident channel or to a webhook endpoint.
[06:48] Ethan: about SDKs — we use TypeScript heavily. how stable is the node SDK? we prefer typed models and streaming types for the frontend.
[06:59] Laura: node SDK is first-class, with TypeScript types. streaming uses an event stream with typed events. the SDKs also have built-in backpressure helpers for streaming use cases.

[07:30] [Laura shares screen briefly; link noted in chat: https://redwood.example.com/langchain-examples]

[07:45] Maya: we use LangChain heavily—RAG pipelines with elasticsearch + s3 for embeddings. can we plug Redwood embeddings into LlamaIndex?
[07:58] Laura: yes, we maintain adapters: LangChain retriever that calls Redwood embeddings endpoint, and a LlamaIndex storage adapter for Redwood vectors. the examples show batch embed workflows and async streaming for embeddings.
[08:20] Ethan: tokenization mismatch concern — we currently do pre-tokenization on our side for cost estimation. do you expose tokenizer info for models?
[08:31] Laura: we expose model tokenization details and there's an endpoint to estimate token counts. we also include estimated token counts in response headers for generation endpoints.

[09:05] Priya: compliance on private deployment — if we go Private/On-prem, do you support air-gapped installs and on-prem KMS?
[09:15] Samir: yes, Private can be air-gapped; we provide an on-prem bundle and support customer-managed KMS/HSM. audit logs can remain in your storage. there is an enterprise onboarding process and extra validation for air-gap.
[09:34] Maya: cost sensitivity—our product team expects significant token volume. how do quantization and model variants factor into cost reduction?
[09:46] Laura: Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per model; we can run a quick eval to show quality/regression. using quantized variants or smaller family models for non-customer-facing paths reduces cost. we also recommend prefix caching for large contexts.
[10:10] Oliver: what's required to run a POC? we want a small pilot—maybe 1-2 routes — with performance numbers.
[10:20] Samir: typical POC is 2-4 weeks: we provision Dedicated trial capacity or Hosted with reserved throughput, run synthetic and real traffic, and collect latency/cost metrics. laura will scope the Dedicated sizing needed for your QPS profile.
[10:38] Ethan: for the gateway, i'll need an example proxy config for kong/ingress and the recommended headers to pass—auth headers, billing tags, route ids.
[10:49] Laura: i'll share a kong config snippet and recommended headers: x-rw-route, x-rw-project, x-rw-tenant for billing and rate-limits; x-rw-scope for quotas. we'll also provide mTLS client cert examples for Dedicated.

[11:15] Maya: any gotchas with streaming and reconnections? we have flaky mobile networks.
[11:25] Laura: streaming supports reconnection tokens; the SDK has idempotency keys and resume points for streaming. if you lose a connection, the client can resume within a short TTL. we recommend short-lived tokens for mobile.

[12:05] [Minor crosstalk as someone gets coffee]

[12:40] Priya: data retention policy specifics—we need 90 days of logs retained in our region and ability to delete on demand.
[12:53] Samir: Hosted default retention is 30 days, but we can extend in hosted for customers; Dedicated/Private gives you full control. deletion on demand supported with GDPR-style erase endpoints—will include in security doc.

[13:20] Ethan: about observability hooks again—how granular are the traces? can we break down token time into kernel/runtime vs queue?
[13:33] Laura: yes, traces include queue time, kernel exec time, token decode time, and network. you can instrument per-route sampling rates to limit telemetry volume.

[14:05] Oliver: competition question—we've spoken to Anthropic for safety squad features. how does Redwood support guardrails?
[14:16] Samir: Redwood has output filters and rule-based policies you can attach per-route. you can also implement evals with our rollout tooling to monitor quality regressions and auto-rollback.

[14:40] Maya: we need a checklist for security review to give to procurement. can we get a one-pager with SOC2 scope, KMS, and data flow diagram?
[14:51] Laura: yes i'll attach the security one-pager and data flow diagram.

[15:10] Ethan: question re: embeddings — we store vectors in our elasticsearch; do you recommend using Redwood vector store or our existing infra?
[15:22] Laura: both are fine. if you want lower latency and managed index features use Redwood vectors; if you need full control and existing indices, use our embedding endpoint and store vectors in ES. we have examples for both.

[15:50] Maya: small detail — rate-limits per route vs per API key matters for our multi-tenant merchants. do you support per-merchant quotas?
[16:02] Laura: yes, per-tenant quotas are supported. you can set rate-limits on route+tenant and have billing tags so usage is attributed.

[16:30] [Laura pastes a link to a demo repo in chat: https://github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-redwood-examples]

[16:45] Priya: will there be an audit trail of who accessed what prompt? we need user-level audit for compliance.

[16:56] Samir: audit logs include caller identity if you pass along user identifiers in headers; for Hosted we can limit retention or redact content. with Dedicated/Private you keep logs in your account.

[17:20] Ethan: network egress—if we use Dedicated in a cloud region, does traffic leave our VPC?

[17:31] Laura: Dedicated can be deployed inside your VPC for private networking; otherwise traffic goes over secure links. we'll map options in the doc.

[18:00] Oliver: timeline—if we wanted to move to Dedicated for production, what's onboarding lead time?

[18:09] Samir: typically 4-8 weeks depending on compliance checks and capacity reservations. Private on-prem is longer due to air-gap validation.

[18:30] Maya: are there usage examples for cost optimization? we want to run a secondary cheap model for suggested answers and only call a higher-quality model for final responses.

[18:43] Laura: that's a common pattern — route-level fallback to smaller model or cached answer. Redwood Optimize can suggest model/quantization combos based on evals.

[19:10] [Longer pause while attendees skim a shared doc]

[19:50] Samir: recap — we'll send: hosted vs dedicated cost/latency doc, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, kong proxy config, and security one-pager. you (astra) will share traffic profile and sample prompts. then schedule SE-led POC scoping.

[20:12] Maya: yes that's good. one more — we have internal policy that any vendor must support SSO (SAML) and SCIM for provisioning.

[20:26] Priya: and we require IP allowlists for admin consoles.

[20:33] Samir: we support SAML, SCIM, RBAC and admin IP allowlist for both Hosted (via SSO enterprise plan) and Dedicated/Private with customer-managed identity. i'll include configuration notes.

[20:55] Laura: next steps I'll send the integration repo and connect you with our POC specialist.

[21:05] Ethan: for the POC, i want a minimal deployment guide for kong and sample k8s manifest for the sidecar proxy.

[21:15] Laura: will do; i'll include a k8s sidecar example and an ingress snippet.

[21:30] Oliver: are there any sticky legal terms we should expect—data processing addendum, indemnity items?

[21:40] Samir: standard DPA and security addendum; indemnity is standard commercial language. legal will share a redline if needed.

[21:58] Maya: ok thanks everyone — excited to try the hosted pilot then scope Dedicated.

[22:10] Samir: great thanks all — we'll follow up with the pack. Laura and i will send the artifacts by Thursday. any final questions?

[22:22] Priya: nothing else from security.

[22:26] Ethan: all good.

[22:30] Laura: thanks, bye.

[22:40] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had several mis-attributions and some words like "KV cache" appeared as "K V cache" or "K V cash" in early drafts; proper nouns like Kong sometimes transcribed as "cong". timestamps are approximate and inserted every 30-90s for readability.
